title: Negative translation of classical first-order proofs

based_on.title: The Proof Theory of Classical and Constructive Inductive Definitions: A 40 year saga (Pohlersfest lecture, July 18, 2008)

summary: Translate classical first-order proof trees into constructive ones, including equality, protected quantifiers and transformed assumptions.
abstract: A classical proof may use a contradiction to conclude a formula that constructive logic cannot infer directly. Negative translation changes the formula so that this classical step can be replaced by constructive reasoning. We extend the propositional construction through both first-order quantifiers and logical equality, keeping the actual terms and protected parameters. The translated formulas have explicit double-negation elimination proofs, and every classical proof becomes an intuitionistic proof from translated assumptions. A reverse classical conversion gives exact consequence correspondences, while a quantified excluded-middle example explains why one outer double negation does not suffice.
